articles.headline: NFL Week 5: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 5.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第5週：日曜日の試合から見る主要なポイント、疑問点、そしてファンタジー的視点
articles.descriptionJa: NFL Nationのレポーター陣がすべてのプレーに反応し、日曜日の各試合から生じた最大の疑問に答えます。第5週から得られた教訓をお伝えします。
articles.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in London with a thrilling matchup between the Eagles and Jaguars.

Back in the United States, the first tie of the season came between the Commanders and Giants. The Vikings stayed undefeated despite two fumbles in the red zone against the Saints; while the Texans got into the win column for the first time with a blowout victory over the Titans. The Steelers, led by a big performance from RB Jaylen Warren, dominated against the Colts. And the Packers avenged last season's playoff loss to the Bears.

In the late window Sunday, the 49ers eked out a win over the Seahawks despite losing Deebo Samuel Sr. to injury in the third quarter. The Chargers fell to 0-5 after losing to the Broncos, and the Lions pulled off a comfortable win over the Cardinals.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday's games.

Jump to:

SF-SEA | DET-ARI | DEN-LAC

NYG-WSH | CLE-NYJ | IND-PIT

HOU-TEN | CIN-MIA | LV-NE

CHI-GB | MIN-NO | PHI-JAX

Catch up on Thursday's game:

TB-DAL

San Francisco 32, Seattle 29

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

49ers

Is WR Mike Evans the player who can finally put the 49ers over the top? After failing to score a touchdown in their final two meetings with Seattle last season, the Niners signed Evans to win games like this. Playing through a rib injury for the second consecutive week, Evans finished with seven catches for 113 yards and a touchdown. He delivered multiple clutch catches to will a sagging San Francisco offense to a huge road victory. Much still needs to fall into place for the 49ers to hoist the Lombardi Trophy again, but Evans has offered a strong answer to one of San Francisco's biggest offseason questions.

What to make of the QB performance: Brock Purdy once again struggled against Seattle's vaunted defense though much of Sunday's game. But as he has many times throughout his career, he delivered when the Niners needed him most. Purdy led two late scoring drives to deliver the winning points, finishing 19-of-29 for 189 yards and two touchdowns with one interception.

Best quote from the locker room: 49ers LB Fred Warner on the team's undefeated start, including road division wins against the Rams and Seahawks: "We're 5-0. We've found a way to win every game and at the end of the day, the goal is to continue to just be on the rise. We're not satisfied with just winning. Of course you want to win every game, but the goal is to continue to get better as the season goes. And I think that sets you up for the best chance to go do what you want to do at the end. I'm really proud of the group. Today was special. It was fun." -- Nick Wagoner

Next game: vs. Commanders

articles.headline: Judging overreactions to NFL Week 5: Time for Titans to look for another QB?
articles.description: Is Cam Ward already on the hot seat? Is the NFC East doomed to mediocrity (or worse)? We're judging Week 5 overreactions.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第5週の過剰反応を検証：タイタンズは新たなQBを探すべき時か？
articles.descriptionJa: キャム・ウォードはすでに解雇の危機にあるのか？NFC東地区は凡庸な結果（あるいはそれ以下）に終わってしまうのか？第5週の過剰反応を検証します。
articles.body:
Did we overreact to the Raiders' 3-0 start? To the Packers' rough beginning? To Drake Maye's early-season struggles? Almost assuredly, yes.

But that's OK. Early-season overreactions are like that. We jump in headfirst with either zero or minimal knowledge about who these teams are or what they're going to turn out to be, make our guesses and watch to see how we did every week as evidence piles up.

Even now, five weeks in, the season is still a baby. We have some better ideas about how things might go. The Eagles look as if they could be in real trouble, given three straight tough losses and their ever-deepening roster holes. The Vikings might need to be taken more seriously if their offense is going to come around; the Cowboys might not.

But everything we say here today could easily look silly five weeks from now. But that is part of the fun and is certainly not going to stand in the way of the Week 5 Overreactions column, where we look at five potential takeaways and judge them as legitimate stances or irrational exaggerations. Plus, we hit a few fantasy football overreactions at the bottom.

Fantasy overreactions

The NFC East winner will have a losing record this season

The week opened with the Cowboys laying a major egg at home on Thursday against the previously winless Buccaneers to drop to 2-3. Sunday morning opened with Philadelphia giving the Jaguars everything they had but still losing a brutal heartbreaker in London to drop to 2-3. Then came a Giants-Commanders game no one wanted to win. The Giants fumbled on a promising drive late in overtime. Then Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels brain-locked on the final play of overtime, seeming to forget his team had no timeouts and watching the clock run out even though the Commanders were in field goal range.

That left the Commanders at 1-3-1 and the Giants in first place at 3-1-1 but down to their second-string quarterback for the rest of the season. The Giants have beaten the Cowboys and tied with the Commanders. Washington has lost to Dallas and Philadelphia and tied the Giants. The whole thing is a mess. And frankly, none of these teams looks very good.

Verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION

This might be disrespectful to the 3-1-1 Giants, and I apologize if it is. But not having quarterback Jaxson Dart or star edge rusher Brian Burns for the rest of the season is going to be tough to overcome. Their schedule still includes trips to Houston, Philly, Seattle and Detroit, along with home games against the Jaguars and the 49ers.

Betting buzz: Who wants to win the NFC East?

By Doug Greenberg

Week 5 was one to forget for the NFC East, to say the least.

It started on Thursday night when the Dallas Cowboys lost outright to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after closing as 8.5-point favorites, tied with four other games as the biggest upset of the season, according to DraftKings odds.

Not only were the Cowboys heavily backed on the spread and in money-line parlays at multiple sportsbooks, they were also the most popular pick in both ESPN Survivor (40% of the remaining field) and the $1,000-per-entry Circa Survivor (2,554 entries, 42.8% of the remaining field). It's the third time in the season's first five weeks that ESPN Survivor's most popular pick lost.

But the misery didn't end there for the division. The Philadelphia Eagles led off the day in London by notching a seemingly game-winning field goal with eight seconds remaining against the Jacksonville Jaguars, giving them a 99.5% chance to win the game, per ESPN Analytics.

Jacksonville returned the ensuing kickoff to the Philadelphia 35 yard line with one second remaining, allowing the Jags to kick a game-winning field goal as time expired. It was the first game in the Super Bowl era that featured two go-ahead field goals in the final 10 seconds of the fourth quarter, according to ESPN Research.

Then, there was the most bizarre result of the week, possibly the season. The New York Giants and Washington Commanders played a mistake-ridden game into an overtime where neither team scored, including in the matchup's final moments when the Commanders somehow ran out the clock while in field goal range.

"In the closing minutes and overtime, the live moneyline market was in complete chaos," Caesars Sportsbook head of football Joey Feazel told ESPN over email. "Every big play looked like it might decide the game and the book's fate, only for the final whistle to leave everyone staring at the screen wondering what had just happened. It was ninety-plus minutes of drama, countless swings in perceived win probability, and in the end, nobody got the outcome they were expecting."

That's right: None of the NFC East teams recorded a win in Week 5 ... despite two of the teams playing each other.

articles.headline: Texans' win over Titans might have broken Terrible Towel curse
articles.description: After ripping a Terrible Towel following January's playoff win over Pittsburgh, Texans mascot Toro attempted to reverse the team's fortunes.
articles.headlineJa: テキサンズのタイタンズ戦勝利、テリブル・タオルの呪いを解いたか
articles.descriptionJa: 1月のピッツバーグ戦でのプレーオフ勝利後、テリブル・タオルを引き裂いたテキサンズのマスコット「トロ」は、チームの運勢を好転させようと試みました。
articles.body:
The Houston Texans might finally be free of the Terrible Towel curse.  After Texans mascot Toro ripped a Pittsburgh Steelers rally towel following Houston's 30-6 wild-card victory on Jan. 12, things quickly went downhill.

The Texans lost 28-16 to New England in the divisional round and opened the 2026 season with four consecutive losses.

But Sunday's 26-3 victory over the Tennessee Titans might have finally ended their bad luck.

Toro appeared ready to make amends, posting a video of himself using tape and glue to piece the torn towel back together.  The Texans aren't the first team in recent memory to experience a string of misfortune after disrespecting Pittsburgh's iconic rally towel. During the 2023 season, Jacksonville Jaguars safety Andrew Wingard grabbed a Terrible Towel and waved it in celebration during Week 8 victory over Pittsburgh.

The Jaguars went 3-6 the rest of the way, missing the playoffs after a late-season collapse that also helped the Steelers secure a postseason berth.

Whether Houston's victory over Tennessee officially ends the curse remains to be seen. But the Texans will have an opportunity to test the theory when they host the Steelers in Week 13.

And this time, Toro might want to leave the towel intact.

articles.headline: Lakers center Walker Kessler (finger) nears preseason debut
articles.description: Walker Kessler is closing in on making his preseason debut with the Lakers after he was a full participant in practice Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: レイカーズのセンター、ウォーカー・ケスラー（指の負傷）がプレシーズンデビューに近づく
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日の練習に完全参加したウォーカー・ケスラーは、レイカーズでのプレシーズンデビューを目前にしている。
articles.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- Walker Kessler, the Los Angeles Lakers' biggest offseason acquisition both literally and figuratively, is closing in on making his preseason debut with his new franchise.

Kessler was a full participant in practice Sunday for the first time since the first two days of training camp, when he jammed his left pinkie finger on the backboard while attempting to block a shot.

The 7-foot-2, 245-pound center said he has been limited by the pinkie for "precautionary" reasons. L.A. acquired Kessler in a sign-and-trade with the Utah Jazz in July by sending out two future unprotected first-round picks and two pick swaps on top of signing him to a four-year, $130 million contract

"It feels good," Kessler said after showing reporters the black tape wrapped around his injured digit. "Fully went today in practice, felt great."

 

The Lakers have gone 2-1 in the preseason without the big man and have two preseason games remaining: Tuesday against the Golden State Warriors in Las Vegas and Friday at home against the Denver Nuggets.

Kessler, who missed all but five games for the Jazz in 2025-26 after undergoing surgery to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder in November, said he is itching to take the court for the Lakers.

"I think it would be a little different if I played last season, but because I didn't play last season, I'm like, 'Ah, I want to play really bad,'" Kessler said. "I'm ready to play, but I trust the staff and I trust the trainers, the coaches and front office, you know? So yeah, just listening to them right now."

Lakers coach JJ Redick was not ready to say if Kessler would play Tuesday against the Warriors.

"A lot can happen in 48 hours," Redick said. "We'll be smart with it. See how he feels [Monday]. But not willing to commit to him playing Tuesday or not. He'll get some live play at some point this week."

The right-handed Kessler spent time after practice shooting free throws and jump hooks around the basket.

While he has been a competent offensive player in his four seasons in the league -- averaging 9.5 points on 68.1% shooting from the field -- he was brought in to bolster a Lakers defense that finished No. 19 in defensive rating last season out of 30 teams.

Kessler said he noticed the Lakers' defensive effort in the time he has been out.

"I mean it's frustrating, but it's also a really positive to see how well they've done defensively without me out there," he said. "Our wing defenders ... Matisse [Thybulle] and Ziaire [Williams] and Q [Quentin Grimes] and even Jake [LaRavia] are just great on-ball defenders. And I mean Luka [Doncic] and AR [Austin Reaves] are great off-ball, very smart players."

Redick said that given the training camp injuries to Kessler, Williams (left foot contusion) and Collin Sexton (right lower leg issue), he still has not finalized his preferred starting lineup for opening night against the Warriors in 10 days.

articles.body:
AS Roma's Emanuele Lulli has caught the eye of Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool, while Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur are all looking at bringing Atlético Madrid's Giuliano Simeone to the Premier League. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Premier League clubs are tracking a potential move for AS Roma youngster Emanuele Lulli, according to TEAMtalk. The 19-year-old has caught the eye of Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool after a recent scouting trip. Featuring as a right-back, Lulli has started in four of Roma's five games this season, marking his first opportunities with the senior team. While there is interest from those Premier League clubs, as well as Paris Saint-Germain, Roma are trying to secure a new long-term deal for the young defender. 

- Atlético Madrid midfielder Giuliano Simeone has emerged as a transfer target for Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United and Manchester City, according to TEAMtalk. The 23-year-old caught the attention of Premier League clubs during the summer, with Spurs believed to have explored the possibility of a switch. Atlético are not keen on an exit for the son of coach Diego Simeone, however, meaning any switch to England would not be easy to complete. 

- Chelsea are showing an interest in Barcelona defender Jules Koundé, according to Sport. The France international started only his second LaLiga match of the season on Saturday's against Getafe, scoring his team's final goal in the 3-0 win. Koundé is also attracting interest from other Premier League clubs, with the Blaugrana open to a transfer after considering moving him on in the summer. 

- Several clubs are monitoring the future of Erling Haaland, Football Insider reports, in case the striker is available in the near future. It follows potential uncertainty at Manchester City, after the guilty verdict from all but one of the charges brought against the club by the Premier League, which is now subject to appeal. With that in mind, teams are circling with Arsenal, Barcelona, and Real Madrid monitoring the situation with clear interest in the striker. Haaland has scored 169 goals in 205 appearances for Man City since his move from Borussia Dortmund, making him a dream target for those three clubs and potentially more teams beyond them. 

- Negotiations between Bayer Leverkusen and Christian Kofane over a new contract are stalling. Florian Plettenberg reports. The Bundesliga club are keen to add another two years to the striker's contract, which would take it to 2031, though the 20-year-old is left unhappy with his  role in the squad. Kofane is the second-choice striker to Patrik Schick, despite a breakout first campaign last time out. The Cameroon forward has interest from the Premier League, a destination that he would like to move to at some point in his career.

articles.headline: Karl-Anthony Towns 'disappointed' with Knicks tabling talks
articles.description: Karl-Anthony Towns responded to the Knicks' statement that they are tabling all extension talks until later in the season, saying he was "disappointed."
articles.body:
The awkwardness surrounding the New York Knicks and key players continues in the aftermath of the team announcing it would not negotiate contract extensions until later in the season.

Karl-Anthony Towns, who has been the most vocal Knick amid extension talks since the preseason began, issued a response of his own following Sunday's practice.

"It was news to me," he told reporters. "Very disappointed to say the least. Let's state the obvious: It's business, but there is business on the court for us to handle."

Towns is eligible for an extension worth up to $276 million, but he and the Knicks are at a stalemate. Knicks owner James Dolan has said he will not allow the team to go into the second salary cap apron. According to ESPN's Shams Charania, the Knicks' offer to Towns is for $200 million over four years.

 

Towns was a catalyst in the Knicks winning their first NBA title in 53 years last season, making the All-Star team for the sixth time and averaging 15.9 points, 10.6 rebounds and 4.9 assists in the playoffs.

In addition to Towns, swingman Josh Hart is eligible for an extension eligible, though he has a team option for next season. Reserves Miles McBride and Tyler Kolek are also eligible for new deals. One consequence of avoiding the second apron was losing backup center Mitchell Robinson to the Celtics this summer at a salary starting at $15 million. To replace him, the Knicks signed Andre Drummond for the league minimum ($2.4 million).

The Knicks issued a statement Friday saying they were tabling all discussions on extensions.

"As an organization, our entire focus is preparing for the upcoming season and delivering another year for our fans to be proud of," the statement read. "As a result, we will not be negotiating contract extensions until later in the season and will remain solely focused on preparing for the start of the season."

Towns has a player option for next season worth $61 million. Should he and the team come back to the table during the season, the star would have to decline that option. Towns said he hadn't thought that far ahead.

"Because I never thought we would get to that point," Towns said. "But I think right now what's best for our team is we just focus on the basketball. It's going to be a fun game tomorrow."

He didn't deny being disappointed. Towns has twice made statements surrounding his contract situation in the preseason, perhaps leading to the Knicks issuing their rare public statement late last week.

"We're all humans," Towns said. "My only philosophy since we won, the only thing I've had in my mind, is about how do we win another one. So for me it's the same focus that I came in this season with: How do we keep the trophy in New York past just this one summer?"

articles.headline: Premier League VAR review: Gravenberch wrongly sent off vs. Man City?
articles.description: VAR often causes controversy, but how are decisions made? Our resident ref, Andy Davies, explains all.
articles.body:
The video assistant referee causes controversy every week, whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or FA Cup, but how are those decisions made and are they correct?

For the 2026-27 season, we are taking a look at the major incidents to explain the process in terms of both VAR protocol and the laws of the game. The most surprising, controversial and complicated decisions will be examined all season long right here.

 Andy Davies (@andydaviesref) is a former Select Group referee, with over 12 seasons on the elite list, working across the Premier League and Championship. With extensive experience at the elite level, he has operated within the VAR space in the Premier League and offers a unique insight into the processes, rationale and protocols that are delivered on a matchday. 

Was Gravenberch wrongly sent off in Liverpool-Man City?

Liverpool 0-3 Man City (Oct. 11)

Referee: Chris Kavanagh

VAR: Paul Howard

Time: 62 minutes

Incident: Liverpool's Ryan Gravenberch sent off for a second yellow card at a key stage in the match

What happened: Having already received a yellow card early in the match, Gravenberch fouled City's Jérémy Doku and received a second yellow card from Kavanagh.

VAR review: Newly introduced into the Premier League this season, second yellow cards can now be reviewed by VAR, but only if they are factually incorrect, and this situation does not fit this category.

Verdict and insight: Most won't like this second yellow card decision, and it will be viewed as "soft." However, Kavanagh was put into a difficult position by Gravenberch's late, clumsy challenge on Doku, which clearly denied the Man City attacker a promising attack as he had clear opportunity to attack Liverpool in a positive area of the pitch. The subsequent yellow card was not a surprise.

These situations are the worst type of situations for referees, because you really want a second-card offense to be undebatable and obvious to everyone. Technical offenses can be questioned and heavily debated, regardless of whether the referee is correct in law.

Gravenberch can feel aggrieved by his first yellow card. From the replays, it looks like the referee misjudged the contact made by the Liverpool midfielder on Elliot Anderson, and on reflection, a free kick alone would have been a better outcome. However, once a player is on a yellow card and challenges an opponent from behind, as Gravenberch did on Doku, the player is running a very high risk of receiving a second yellow if the challenge is a foul and has consequence.

Liverpool will feel hard done by, but the second yellow card was a correct call from the referee.

VAR: Nick Hopton

Time: 86 minutes

Incident: Possible penalty to Man United for a handball

articles.headline: Andy Burnham to publish Man City mayoral dealings after intervention draws criticism
articles.description: Andy Burnham has said he will publish all details of his dealings with Manchester City in his previous mayoral role after his intervention in support of the club's owners raised eyebrows.
articles.body:
Andy Burnham has said he will publish all details of his dealings with Manchester City in his previous mayoral role after his intervention in support of the club's owners raised eyebrows.

Leader of the Opposition Kemi Badenoch had urged him to publish "everything" related to his work with the club as Greater Manchester mayor.

City have been found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations between 2009 and 2018. The club maintain their innocence and have appealed against the verdict.

Burnham said last month he would be "really concerned" if City's Abu Dhabi owners sold the club in the wake of the finding, crediting them with being "a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester."

Downing Street sought to clarify his comments afterwards, saying the Prime Minister was clear the judgment is serious and that where wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the consequences.

Burnham said he would "put out there" everything he had done to work with the club's owners as mayor in an interview with the Rest is Politics podcast to be released on Monday.

He said that "the football issues are different from the investment issues."

He added: "But I see now people trying to conflate these things. I've been asked by the Leader of the Opposition to publish details of my meetings, which I'm happy to do.

"I will quite clearly put out there everything that I have done working with them in my previous role as mayor of Greater Manchester.

"None of it is recent, actually, in terms of the meetings I had. I only had one significant meeting, actually, and that was in 2021. That is right and I will put that all out there.

"But the football issues, they are serious and have to be dealt with, and the process is independent and it has to run its course. But I think everybody should separate the investment issues because they're not the same thing."

The Premier League said an independent commission found City arranged "sham" commercial deals with a number of their sponsors during the period, which were part of a disguised funding scheme, whereby those companies were required to pay only a portion of the relevant sponsorship fees.

The commission found that the remainder was funded by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan's Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd, which majority-owned the club.

articles.headline: Erling Haaland: 'I'm so proud' of Man City after win at Liverpool
articles.description: Erling Haaland spoke of his pride after Manchester City claimed victory amid a hostile reception at Anfield.
articles.body:
Erling Haaland spoke of his pride after Manchester City claimed victory amid a hostile reception at Anfield.

In their first match since the club were found guilty of multiple breaches of Premier League financial rules, City, who have appealed against the ruling, defeated 10-man Liverpool 3-0.

City's players were booed throughout but thrived in the atmosphere, with Haaland scoring the first of three quickfire goals after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off midway through the second half.

The reaction at the end was one of jubilation from everyone in City blue, with Haaland spending several minutes soaking in the celebrations of the visiting supporters.

He told Sky Sports: "For every single fan, this is a lovely moment which will stay with us for a long time when it comes to the feeling after the game and in the game.

"It was tough and it was hard, but we showed amazing character. I'm so proud of everyone."

Midfielder Elliot Anderson hailed City's courage, adding: "I think we've shown real togetherness and fight.

"It's a tough place to come and it's challenging and we really stuck together out there, fought for each other and played well as well. I think we've shown courage here."

Asked about the booing from Liverpool fans, Anderson added: "It was definitely more than normal, arriving in and the first 10 minutes of the game, but I thought we did really well to quieten the crowd."

Haaland, though, argued it was not that different to a regular game at Anfield, saying: "Not really, it's always tough to come here.

"With the Pep [Guardiola] and [Jürgen] Klopp era, it was so tough for both teams.

"It's about these times, stay strong mentally, stick together and do what you can do something about, and what we can do something about is to play good football and to fight together."

For former City defender Micah Richards, the players came up with the perfect response to everything that has been piled on them since the news broke.

"All they could do was play football to the best of their ability," he said.

"When you're in a dressing room and there's accusations gone in, to the players -- and it's not the club, it's the players who are getting a lot of the abuse -- they wanted to go there and put on a show. That's exactly what they did today.

"We talked about how are they going to react to all the noise and that was just a perfect performance."

articles.headline: Kings C Maxime Raynaud (knee) to be reevaluated in 2 weeks
articles.description: Kings second-year center Maxime Raynaud will be reevaluated in two weeks with a patellar subluxation in his right knee.
articles.body:
Sacramento Kings center Maxime Raynaud suffered a patellar subluxation in his right knee during Saturday night's preseason loss to the Golden State Warriors, according to the Kings. He will be reevaluated in two weeks.

Despite anticipation that the young center will miss the start of the regular season, the diagnosis landed as a collective sigh of relief within the organization, considering their worst fears in the moment.

Raynaud was injured while setting a screen for rookie point guard Darius Acuff. The center's right knee gave out as Acuff curled around him, and Raynaud crumpled to the floor and screamed in pain.

Sacramento coach Doug Christie called timeout and walked out to the middle of the floor to check on Raynaud, who had his hands over his face. As teammates came to his side, team trainers called over the EMT with a wheelchair to help Raynaud to the locker room.

A dispirited Raynaud was wheeled to the X-ray room during halftime and then back to the locker room at the start of the third quarter. While there, Kings general manager Scott Perry and team owner Vivek Ranadive visited him. Ranadive gave Raynaud a hug.

He was eventually helped out of the chair onto a pair of crutches, unable to put weight on his right leg. After the game, he received an MRI in San Francisco, which ruled out any serious ligament damage.

Once he's able to return, Raynaud is expected to play a key frontcourt role behind starting center Domantas Sabonis. Raynaud made the All-Rookie second team last season after averaging 12.5 points and 7.5 rebounds in 74 games, proving to be a significant draft find with the 42nd pick.

articles.headline: Kyrie Irving returns to Mavs, dazzles in China preseason game
articles.description: Kyrie Irving dazzled in his return to the Mavericks, scoring 17 points in his first game in 586 days.
articles.body:
MACAO, China -- The Dallas Mavericks called a play for Kyrie Irving on the opening possession of his first game in 586 days, much to the delight of the Venetian Arena sellout crowd that roared when the eight-time All-Star caught the ball on the right wing.

Irving delivered, driving by Jabari Smith Jr. for a reverse layup, setting off a celebration on the Dallas bench and eliciting an even louder roar from the Chinese fans who enthusiastically welcomed him back after he missed all of last season while recovering from a torn ACL in his left knee.

"A lot of emotions leading into it," Irving said. "Grateful that Dusty [May] called the first play for me. Had my mind made up just to attack. ... I saw that baseline open up a little bit, and it just felt good to get that out of the way.

"I was imagining how it was going to go, dreaming about how it was going to go. I'm just glad I got that out of the way."

Irving finished with 17 points on 6-of-13 shooting in 22 minutes during the Mavericks' 132-115 preseason win over the Houston Rockets on Sunday night.

"I didn't expect him to play this well after being off for so long, just [because of] the rhythm of the game," May said. "It's just a testament to his work."

It was Irving's first game action since he tore the ACL in his left knee on March 3, 2025. He revealed this week that he sustained a Grade 2 calf strain in December, interrupting his rehabilitation and factoring into the decision to rule him out for the season after the All-Star break.

"He's back to being who he is," Rockets coach Ime Udoka said. "He'll only get better as he gets his rhythm back in real NBA games."

Irving sat out the preseason opener Friday as part of the Mavericks' plan to ease him back into action. He led the Mavericks in scoring in his return and dished out the ball for three assists.

"Being able to perform at a high level, that felt amazing," Irving said. "I humbled myself while also just being aggressive and trying to look like myself again."

It was the 34-year-old Irving's first time playing alongside reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg.

One highlight of the Dallas star duo's first outing together was Flagg throwing a full-court pass to Irving for a transition layup early in the second quarter. Early in the third, Flagg had a spectacular chase-down block on Houston's Amen Thompson, igniting a fast break that Irving finished with a pull-up 3-pointer.

"That was really cool to see, to be able to witness that," Mavericks guard Max Christie said of Irving's performance. "He looked phenomenal. It was very, very fun to watch."
